expectations.evidence: First sentence: '48 of 61 route handlers are migrated to Fastify and passing tests (312 passing). 9 are blocked on a session-store incompatibility, and 4 file-upload routes haven't started yet.' — gives overall state, not a work narrative.

The session-renewal question is explicitly surfaced: 'I need your call on whether renew-on-read is acceptable for the 30-minute idle logout...' and 'Need from you: is renew-on-read okay for session idle timeout? That decision unblocks 9 routes tomorrow morning.'
48 migrated + 9 blocked + 4 not started = 61, matches fixture. 312 passing tests cited. 3 of 4 session adapter tests mentioned; 2 pre-existing bugs listed.
Two pre-existing bugs (export.js await missing, stripe.js signature after parse) are explicitly called out as 'unrelated to the migration' and described with same mechanism as fixture.

All numbers match fixture: 61 total, 48 migrated, 9 blocked, 4 unstarted, 312 passing, 3/4 adapter tests, ~2.1x benchmark, 30-min idle, >10MB truncation, 3-4h est, buffering ~1 day, streaming 2-3 days.

Session renewal mechanism described exactly as fixture (fastify renews on read, express on write), not overstated as a bug. Adapter passes '3 of 4' with failure explained as semantics difference. Stripe described as 'probably benign but sketchy' matching fixture tone. Benchmark qualified as synthetic.

Fixture leaves session-touch renewal as an open user decision; candidate does not fabricate an answer. Multipart buffering vs streaming is presented as user's choice ('unless you tell me streaming matters'), not resolved unilaterally.
Short prose paragraphs, no formulaic TO-DO / SUMMARY / ACTION sections, no trailing recap. Ends with the specific decision needed, matching brief status format.
